title: Dutch Supreme Court orders government to review jet parts export licence to Israel | Reuters
text:
Dutch Supreme Court orders government to review jet parts export licence to Israel | Reuters

- Summary

- Dutch Supreme Court rules on weapons exports to Israel
- It orders government to review weapons export licence
- Government has six weeks to carry out the review
- Ruling keeps ban of export of F-35 parts in place pending review

THE HAGUE, Oct 3 (Reuters) - The Supreme Court of the Netherlands ordered the Dutch government on Friday to review its policies on weapons exports to Israel.

The court did not uphold a ban on the export of parts for F-35 fighter jets ordered by a lower court last year, but it said the government needed to assess whether there was a risk of the jet parts being used in violation of international law.

It gave the government six weeks to carry out this review, during which the export of fighter jet parts would still be banned.
